record.context_brief: Extremal Type II Z_(2k)-codes producing extremal lattices
record.original_question: For lengths n that are multiples of 8, find a Type II self-dual code over Z_(2k), with 2k ≥ 2s + 2, whose minimum Euclidean weight d_E satisfies d_E/(2k) = 2s + 2, so that Construction A yields an extremal unimodular lattice.

evidence.quote: A self-dual code over Z2k where every vector has weight a multiple of 4k is said to be Type II.
Theorem 8.2. ... The minimum norm is min{2k, dE/2k} where dE is the minimum Euclidean weight of C. Moreover, if C is Type II then the lattice Λ(C) is an even unimodular lattice.
Open Question 8.3. In length n, a multiple of 8, find a Type II self-dual code over Z2k, 2k ≥ 2s + 2 such that dE/2k = 2s + 2. Such an extremal code will give an extremal lattice using Theorem 8.2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k\ge 1$ and consider the ring $\mathbb{Z}_{2k}=\mathbb{Z}/2k\mathbb{Z}$. For a vector $x=(x_1,\dots,x_n)\in\mathbb{Z}_{2k}^n$, define its Euclidean weight by
$$\mathrm{wt}_E(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n \min\{x_i^2,(2k-x_i)^2\},$$
where $x_i$ is identified with its representative in $\{0,1,\dots,2k-1\}$. A linear code $C\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{2k}^n$ is self-dual if $C=C^\perp$ with respect to the standard inner product modulo $2k$. The code $C$ is called Type II if it is self-dual and every codeword has Euclidean weight divisible by $4k$. Let $d_E(C)$ denote the minimum nonzero Euclidean weight of $C$.

Construction A assigns to such a code $C$ the lattice
$$\Lambda(C)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2k}}\bigl\{x\in\mathbb{Z}^n : x \bmod 2k \in C\bigr\}.$$
If $C$ is Type II, then $\Lambda(C)$ is an even unimodular lattice of minimum norm $\min\{2k,\,d_E(C)/(2k)\}$. An even unimodular lattice in dimension $n$ (a multiple of $8$) is called extremal if its minimum norm equals $2\lfloor n/24\rfloor+2$.

Problem: Let $n$ be a positive multiple of $8$, and write $s=\lfloor n/24\rfloor$. Construct a Type II self-dual code $C$ over $\mathbb{Z}_{2k}$ of length $n$ with $2k\ge 2s+2$ such that
$$\frac{d_E(C)}{2k}=2s+2,$$
so that $\Lambda(C)$ is an extremal even unimodular lattice. Determine, for each such $n$ and each admissible $k$, whether such an extremal Type II $\mathbb{Z}_{2k}$-code exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a general existence question; constructions are known in many specific cases (e.g., extremal Type II $\mathbb{Z}_{2k}$-codes of length 24 for $k=4,\dots,20$ and length 32 for $k=4,\dots,10$, plus recent constructions for lengths 56 and 64 over $\mathbb{Z}_4$), but the general existence question for all multiples of 8 and admissible $k$ remains open. Results from 2022–2024 continue to address specific cases, indicating the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Construction of extremal Type II Z_{2k}-codes
status_evidence.snippet: Extremal Type II Z_{2k}-codes of length 24 have been constructed for k=4,5,...,20 and of length 32 for k=4,5,...,10.
status_evidence.claim: Many specific cases of the problem have been resolved by explicit constructions.

status_evidence.title: New extremal Type II Z_4-codes of length 64
status_evidence.snippet: New extremal Type II Z_4-codes of lengths 56 and 64 have been constructed.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress continues, but the full question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Extremal Type I Z_k-codes and k-frames of odd unimodular lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Method for constructing m-frames in unimodular lattices via self-dual Z_k-codes.
status_evidence.claim: Related constructions exist but do not settle the general existence.
